title: Cache & Batching Teardown — Guided Tutorial and Decision Walkthrough
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a guided, interactive teardown experience in the Redwood Console that walks platform/ML engineers through request fingerprints and workload slices to produce conservative caching and batching recommendations. The teardown is a hands-on tutorial inside the Console: users start from a route or model dashboard, inspect representative request traces, flag risky token prefixes, and step through suggested config changes with explainers, cost delta estimates, and rollback playbooks. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by surfacing safe-first recommendations and show trade-offs so teams can run controlled rollouts without disrupting SLOs.
scope: Design flow and hi-fi prototype for a 3-step guided teardown: (1) Select workload slice and view fingerprint summary, (2) Run 'What-if' simulator to preview batching/cache effects, (3) Apply recommendation with canary rollout and auto-guardrails. Deliverables: Figma prototype, annotated spec with acceptance criteria, developer handoff notes, and a short test script for early dogfooders.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Figma prototype covering the three-step teardown flow and all primary states (empty, recommendations available, risk flagged, applied with canary)
Simulator shows estimated latency and token-cost deltas for at least three example slices; numbers are validated by ENG during handoff
Microcopy explains each suggested change (why, safety trade-offs, expected gain) in plain language and includes quick rollback copy
Rollout step includes simple canary toggles, monitoring links to route-level latency/cost dashboards, and an auto-fallback option
Design handoff includes accessibility checks (contrast, keyboard nav) and a short QA checklist for UX and metrics observability
notes: Assume ENG will provide a mocked endpoint for the simulator; prototypes should be data-agnostic and accept CSV samples
We must surface uncertainty bands for cost estimates — e.g., +/- 10% default — until runtime analytics refines them
Keep initial guardrail semantics conservative: only recommend cache prefixes that match >90% request prefix stability
Do not introduce new account-level billing metrics in this iteration; use existing token/cost breakdowns in Console
decisions: Use a guided three-step modal anchored from route/model dashboard instead of a full-page wizard to reduce context switching
Simulator will operate on representative workload slices (example: 1000 sampled requests) instead of entire traffic to keep performance fast
Recommendations will be labeled with a 'safety score' (High/Medium/Low) and suggested rollout type (Canary/Gradual/Disabled)
We will display both absolute and percentage cost deltas to help teams with budgeting conversations
